intro.title: OAuth2 PKCE Flow in a SPA
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a secure login feature for a Single Page Application (SPA) using the OAuth2 Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) flow. You will learn how to generate a secret code verifier, create a challenge from it, and securely exchange an authorization code for an access token. The main technologies you'll use are React with TypeScript for the frontend and the `crypto-js` library for cryptographic operations. By the end, you'll understand how to protect your application from authorization code interception attacks while implementing a real-world authentication pattern.
intro.usecase: The OAuth2 PKCE flow is essential for securing single-page applications that integrate with third-party services like Google, GitHub, or Microsoft. Developers implement this pattern when building dashboards that display data from external APIs, such as analytics platforms showing Google Drive file statistics or project management tools syncing with GitHub repositories. This flow appears in login screens where users authenticate via "Sign in with Google" buttons, ensuring tokens are exchanged securely without exposing secrets. Every modern SPA that accesses protected resources from OAuth2 providers—from fitness apps pulling Strava data to financial dashboards connecting to banking APIs—relies on PKCE to prevent authorization code interception attacks.
